lines:
Responsibilities: Parses extension manifests without execution, reports discovery and handshake facts to the trusted core registry, and launches/invokes only an explicitly enabled, compatible, exact version/hash contribution authorized for the current host generation. It supplies a language-neutral subprocess protocol for plugin nodes, tools, providers, evaluators, and adapters.
Owned runtime state: ephemeral ExtensionManifestV1 parse results, PluginProtocolSessionV1, handshake/contribution schema cache, child execution handles, request correlation, health, restart backoff observation, and bounded logs. Installed/enabled identity records remain core-owned.
Versioned ports and contracts: ExtensionManifestV1 declares identity, version, Aworkit range, entry point, contributions, schemas, dependencies, and provenance; PluginHandshakeV1, PluginInvocationV1, PluginRawEventV1, PluginHealthV1, and PluginShutdownV1 form the subprocess protocol. Unknown contribution fields are preserved as opaque evidence when safe.
Failure and degraded behavior: malformed manifest, failed attestation, entry-point disappearance, schema/protocol mismatch, crash, or restart-budget exhaustion blocks new dispatch and reports degradation. A crash after possible side effects becomes uncertain; lifecycle restart never replays that invocation.
Security truthfulness: enabled third-party code runs with the desktop user's OS authority unless an explicit real isolation profile was selected. The subprocess boundary is for dependency/crash lifecycle, not security; plugin code can bypass file, network, secret, and approval brokers or spawn further processes.
Observability, performance, and cross-platform behavior: bounded framed messages/logs, health/handshake/crash/restart metrics, provenance and opacity diagnostics, reserved cancellation capacity, and normalized executable discovery/arguments/environment on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Non-responsibilities: no install/enable/integrity decision, marketplace, workflow rewrite, sandbox claim, authority/approval grant, secret-store access outside leases, automatic uncertain-effect retry, or canonical history commit.

data.name: Trusted Extension Protocol & Lifecycle Manager
data.technology: Rust plugin protocol client with supervised Python, Node, Rust, and native subprocesses
